children: Oil prices extend gains, with Brent crude now above $98 a barrel as escalating attacks in the Middle East fuel fears over prolonged supply disruptions. In early European trading, the global oil benchmark rises 1.5% to $98.45 a barrel, while WTI futures climb 2.7% to $93.93 a barrel. "Markets are increasingly pricing a prolonged Mideast conflict," analysts at Goldman Sachs say. "The options-implied probability of Brent above $100 in March 2027 has risen from around 6% a month ago to about 25%." The U.S. bank raised its oil-price forecasts by $5 a barrel, saying it now sees Brent at $85 a barrel and WTI at $80 a barrel in December, assuming shipping disruptions continue into 2027. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
